neighbours.label: narrative fiction prose in which a character discovers or experiences a plot event
fire: After the storm passed, the boy crept outside and saw that the barn was gone.
When Mara opened the letter, she learned that her father had sold the farm.
Back at the inn, the knight realized that his sword had been stolen.
On the third night, the sailor noticed that the stars were moving the wrong way.
Arriving in the village, the stranger discovered that nobody remembered his name.
As the train pulled away, Ellen understood that she would never see him again.
Waking at dawn, the girl found that the river had frozen solid overnight.
Climbing to the tower, the old priest saw that the bell had cracked in two.
quiet: In the survey, the researchers found that most farms had shrunk in size.
The audit showed that the accounts had been kept correctly.
Engineers concluded that the bridge needed new steel cables.
The census revealed that the village had lost half its people.
Tests confirmed that the water was safe to drink.
Analysts noted that the market had recovered by the spring.
The study suggests that sleep improves memory in adults.
Inspectors reported that the barn met all fire codes.

predictions: story narration of a character's discovery 0.15-0.25; expository 'found that' reports below 0.05
notes: Gate-closed regime dominates (68%). Probe: 'he found that the house had been emptied' 0.220, 'the old woman discovers that her brother is still alive' 0.189; 'The report found that sales had risen' 0.023, 'Studies show that' 0.046, dialogue 0.044-0.095. Expect a weak or failed test.
